items.title: Automate an Excel Report with Python: Summaries, Pivot Tables and Formatting (pandas + openpyxl)
items.description:
Turn a raw table into a finished Excel report with one Python script: totals by city, a month-by-city pivot table, three sheets in one file, bold headers, column widths, a frozen header and a live =SUM totals row. Includes the three mistakes that break almost every first report, and every output on screen is the real result of the code shown.

Install
pip install pandas openpyxl

report.py (full script)
import pandas as pd
from openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill

df = pd.read_csv("orders_clean.csv", parse_dates=["Date"])
df = df[df["Status"] != "cancelled"]
df["Revenue"] = df["Qty"] * df["Price"]
df["Month"] = df["Date"].dt.strftime("%Y-%m")

by_city = df.groupby("City")["Revenue"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False).reset_index()
by_month = df.pivot_table(index="Month", columns="City", values="Revenue",
                          aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)

with pd.ExcelWriter("report.xlsx") as writer:
    by_city.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="By city", index=False)
    by_month.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="By month")
    df.to_excel(writer, sheet_name="Data", index=False)

    for ws in writer.sheets.values():
        for cell in ws[1]:
            cell.font = Font(bold=True, color="FFFFFF")
            cell.fill = PatternFill("solid", fgColor="1F6F5C")
        for col in ws.columns:
            ws.column_dimensions[col[0].column_letter].width = 14
        ws.freeze_panes = "A2"

    ws = writer.sheets["By city"]
    last = ws.max_row
    ws[f"A{last + 1}"] = "Total"
    ws[f"B{last + 1}"] = f"=SUM(B2:B{last})"
    ws[f"A{last + 1}"].font = Font(bold=True)
    for row in ws.iter_rows(min_row=2, min_col=2):
        for cell in row:
            cell.number_format = "#,##0.00"

    for cell in writer.sheets["Data"]["B"]:
        cell.number_format = "yyyy-mm-dd"

print("Saved report.xlsx")

The three mistakes
1. Dates stored as text: .dt fails with "Can only use .dt accessor with datetimelike values". Add parse_dates=["Date"] to read_csv.
2. Two to_excel calls with a file name: the second call replaces the whole file, only the last sheet is left. Use one pd.ExcelWriter and pass writer.
3. Forgetting index=False: pandas writes its row numbers as an extra column ("Unnamed: 0" when you read it back).

Pro tip: a new file every month
from datetime import date
name = f"report_{date.today():%Y-%m}.xlsx"

The data is the cleaned orders file from the previous episode (Clean Messy Data with Python).
